newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Q1 public sector surplus 8.891 bln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Q1 public sector surplus 8.891 bln pesos.

text.p: Mexico generated a public sector surplus of 8.891 billion pesos during the first quarter, Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said on Thursday.
Mexico's budget revenues rose 7.1 percent in the year's first three months, while government spending was up 1.3 percent, Ortiz told a news conference.
He did not say what period was used as a comparison for the numbers, but the Finance Ministry generally uses year-on-year comparisons.
Mexico's budget revenues were 166.43 billion pesos during the first quarter, up mostly because of a 10.5 percent real increase in tax receipts compared to the first quarter of 1996.
Net budget spending, meanwhile, was 154.60 billion pesos, according to a Finance Ministry document.

Mexico's primary public surplus -- the difference between total revenue and expenses, excluding debt servicing charges -- was 34.67 billion pesos. No comparative figures were provided by the Finance Ministry.
Ortiz said Mexico's net financing costs of the public debt during the quarter were 16.5 percent of net total spending.

The federal government's net financial surplus during the first quarter was 6.355 billion pesos, the document said. This figure does not include state-owned companies either under direct or indirect financial control.
Ortiz said Mexico's total public sector external debt at the end of the first quarter was $99.931 billion, while total public debt, including external and internal debt, was 28.70 percent of GDP.
During a question-and-answer session following a presentation of public sector results, Ortiz said he saw higher wages and employment in the second quarter helping boost consumption.
Ortiz said fewer working days during the first quarter had hurt industrial production figures and would also affect first quarter GDP, due out on Monday.
He also said he saw Mexico participating less "intensely" in global capital markets this year compared to last year.
